name: January
focus: Protect standing rabi crops from cold and frost; prepare for summer crops.
sow: Late-sown wheat only in extreme delay
Summer vegetables in nursery (chilli, brinjal, tomato)
Sunflower and summer maize in the south
care: Irrigate wheat at the crown root initiation and tillering stages — do not miss CRI.
Give light irrigation on frost-risk nights; moist soil holds more heat than dry soil.
Earth up potato ridges so tubers are not exposed to light and greening.
Top dress mustard and wheat with the second nitrogen split if not already done.
Harvest sugarcane in the subtropics at peak maturity.
Prune and train fruit trees (mango, guava) before the new flush.
watch: Frost and cold waves damaging young crops and vegetables
Aphids building up on mustard and wheat in warm spells
Late blight in potato and tomato during foggy, humid weather
Powdery mildew on vegetables as days warm up
Termites and rodents in dry fields
irrigation_hint: Light, frequent irrigation is better than heavy flooding in cold weather. Irrigate in the morning so the soil warms during the day.

name: February
focus: Push grain filling and pod development; begin summer crop and nursery work.
sow: Summer maize and groundnut in the south
care: Irrigate wheat at the flowering and milk stages — heat stress from late February is the main risk.
Apply the final nitrogen to potato only if the crop is pale, then stop.
Spray potassium nitrate or a micronutrient mix on vegetables after each picking.
Thin and weed mustard and chickpea before they close the rows.
Prepare land for summer crops with deep ploughing and FYM application.
Harvest early sugarcane in the tropics.
watch: Wheat rust (yellow and brown rust) — scout weekly and spray at the first pustules
Aphids on mustard, wheat and vegetables as the weather warms
Pod borer (Helicoverpa) on chickpea and tomato
Early blight in tomato and potato
Heat spike damaging flowering wheat
irrigation_hint: Wheat and mustard need water at flowering. Do not let the soil dry out now — this stage determines the final yield.

name: March
focus: Harvest rabi crops timely and start the summer (Zaid) season.
sow: Green gram and black gram (summer pulses)
care: Harvest wheat at 14–16% moisture and dry to 12% before storage.
Harvest mustard in the early morning to reduce pod shattering.
Harvest chickpea when pods turn brown — do not let them shatter.
Harvest the remaining sugarcane and take a ratoon if the crop was healthy.
Irrigate summer crops lightly and frequently; mulching is essential.
Start mango orchard irrigation once flowering begins.
watch: Sudden heat rise causing poor grain filling in wheat
Stored-grain pests in wheat and pulses
Thrips and mite flare-ups on vegetables as the weather turns hot
Water shortage for summer crops
Early summer thunderstorms with hail
irrigation_hint: Summer irrigation needs rise sharply. Mulch, use drip, and irrigate in the early morning or evening to cut evaporation losses.

name: April
focus: Conserve water, protect summer crops from heat, and prepare for kharif.
sow: Early kharif nursery in the south
care: Mulch summer crops to conserve soil moisture and reduce soil temperature.
Use drip and schedule irrigation at 3–5 day intervals for sandy soils.
Provide shade or protection for nursery beds and young transplants.
Collect and store rainwater; clean farm ponds and check bunds.
Repair and service irrigation pumps, drip lines and filters before the monsoon.
Apply FYM and prepare compost for kharif sowing.
watch: Heat waves above 40 °C causing flower drop and sunscald
Water scarcity and falling groundwater levels
Mites and thrips multiplying rapidly in dry heat
Leaf curl virus in summer vegetables due to high whitefly
Loo (hot dry wind) damage to young orchards
irrigation_hint: This is the peak water-stress month. Irrigate before dawn, use every water-saving method available, and never let young plants dry out.

name: May
focus: Finish land preparation and buy kharif inputs before the monsoon arrives.
sow: Kharif nursery for rice in the south and east
care: Deep summer ploughing to expose soil-borne pests and pathogens.
Get soil tested now — it takes 2–3 weeks and guides the whole kharif plan.
Buy certified seed, seed treatment chemicals and bio-fertilisers early.
Apply FYM and green manure crops (dhaincha, sunhemp) before the rains.
Clean and repair field bunds, channels and drainage outlets.
Prune mango trees after harvest and apply manure.
watch: Heat wave and delayed monsoon onset
Immediate pre-monsoon pests (shoot fly, stem borer) in early-sown crops
Fake or substandard seed in the market — buy from licensed dealers
Pre-monsoon thunderstorm and hail damage
Whitefly and thrips building up before the rains
irrigation_hint: Use the waiting period to repair water infrastructure. Every day of early land preparation saves water later.

name: June
focus: Sow kharif crops with the monsoon and manage the first 30 critical days.
care: Sow only after 50–75 mm of rain or a pre-sowing irrigation so the seed zone is moist.
Treat seed with fungicide and bio-fertiliser before sowing.
Timely weeding at 20–25 days is the single biggest kharif yield factor.
Avoid sowing in a dry spell forecast — wait for a good soaking rain.
Make drainage channels in the field to remove excess rainwater quickly.
Transplant rice seedlings 21–25 days old for best tillering.
watch: Dry spell after sowing causing poor germination
Shoot fly in late-sown jowar and bajra
Early bacterial blight and blast in rice if it rains heavily after transplanting
White grub in groundnut on light soils
Waterlogging damage in heavy soils
irrigation_hint: If the monsoon lags, give one protective irrigation to save the crop. After heavy rain, drain the field — waterlogging is as damaging as drought.

name: July
focus: Weed, thin and top dress; keep drainage channels open.
sow: Vegetable nursery for kharif and early rabi
care: Complete the first weeding and thinning before the canopy closes.
Apply the first nitrogen top dressing to maize, bajra and rice.
Earth up cotton and maize to prevent lodging in heavy rain.
Keep drains clear and drain waterlogged patches within 24 hours.
Stake young fruit plants and vegetable crops against wind.
Rogue out diseased and off-type plants early.
watch: Bacterial blight in rice after storms
Fall armyworm in young maize whorls
Downy mildew in bajra during humid weather
Stem rot and collar rot in soybean if water stands
Nutrient leaching in sandy soils after heavy rain
irrigation_hint: Drainage matters more than irrigation this month. Open the outlets after every heavy spell and check for standing water in low spots.

name: August
focus: Protect flowering crops and manage pest and disease pressure.
sow: Short-duration pulses after early kharif harvest
care: Apply the second nitrogen top dressing at the flowering or knee-high stage.
Monitor pod borer, fruit borer and bollworm with pheromone traps.
Spray protectively before long cloudy, humid spells break out disease.
Remove and destroy pest-affected shoots in brinjal and chilli.
Drain excess water and keep the crop from suffering at flowering.
Top dress long-duration sugarcane.
watch: Blast and sheath blight in rice during humid, cloudy weather
Bollworm and pink bollworm in cotton
Tikka leaf spot in groundnut
Turcicum leaf blight and rust in maize
Continuous rain preventing spraying — plan for rain-free windows
irrigation_hint: The crop is at its most water-sensitive stage. Do not allow a dry spell at flowering — a single protective irrigation can save 20–30% of the yield.

name: September
season: Kharif (grain filling) and early rabi sowing
focus: Grain filling of kharif crops and sowing of early rabi crops.
care: Protect grain filling from moisture stress and pests.
Plan the rabi crop and buy seed before the October rush.
Continue protective sprays for rust and blight in late kharif crops.
Prepare rabi land and incorporate the previous crop residue.
Start onion rabi nursery and vegetable nurseries for the winter.
Harvest early kharif pulses and fodder.
watch: Late-season rust in groundnut and soybean
Armyworm and grasshoppers in maturing cereals
Weevil and storage pest damage on early harvested grain
Cytoplasmic male sterility issues in late kharif hybrids
Heavy late-September rain damaging maturing crops
irrigation_hint: Kharif grain filling still needs moisture. If September turns dry, give one irrigation at grain filling to protect the yield.

name: October
focus: Harvest kharif, sow rabi on time and manage residue.
care: Harvest kharif crops at the correct moisture and dry thoroughly.
Sow wheat in the first fortnight of November for the best yield — do not delay.
Treat wheat seed and use a seed drill for uniform depth.
Apply full P and K and one-third N as basal at sowing.
Do not burn crop residue; incorporate it or use it as mulch.
Prepare potato ridges and apply FYM.
watch: Late-sown wheat losing yield for every week of delay
Termites on dry rabi seedbeds
Stored-grain pests in harvested kharif grain
Warm weather triggering aphids before winter sets in
Residue burning and the resulting nutrient loss
irrigation_hint: Pre-sowing irrigation (palewa) ensures good germination and a uniform stand. Do not sow in dry soil and hope for rain.

name: November
focus: Complete rabi sowing and give the first critical irrigations.
care: Complete all rabi sowing by the end of November.
Irrigate wheat at crown root initiation (20–25 days after sowing).
Apply the first top-dressing nitrogen to wheat and mustard.
Earth up potato ridges and irrigate lightly after planting.
Keep a close watch for early aphids and rust.
Protect young vegetable transplants from cold winds with straw covers.
watch: Aphid buildup on mustard and wheat
Yellow rust appearing in cool, humid pockets
Frost early in northern and central India
Water stress at the crown root initiation of wheat
Termites and cutting worms in dry patches
irrigation_hint: Crown root initiation irrigation is the most important single irrigation in wheat. A missed CRI irrigation can cost 20% of the yield.

name: December
focus: Protect crops from cold and manage pest and disease pressure.
sow: Nothing major; only late planting in warmer regions
care: Light irrigation on frost-risk nights raises soil temperature and protects the crop.
Apply the second nitrogen split to wheat and mustard with irrigation.
Spray potassium and micronutrients on vegetables to fight cold stress.
Harvest sugarcane and start ratoon management in the tropics.
Cover nurseries at night and remove the cover during the day.
Clean and store farm machinery and repair implements.
watch: Frost and cold waves damaging mustard, potato and vegetables
Late blight in potato and tomato in foggy weather
Powdery mildew on vegetables
Fog reducing photosynthesis and delaying grain filling
Aphids and painted bug on mustard
irrigation_hint: In cold weather irrigate in the morning so the soil warms during the day. Avoid late-evening irrigation on frost nights.
